feat(pathkernel): one region model for selection, material side and bounds

Stage 1 of the path kernel (K1). `region(sel, material, bounds, plane,
tool, leave)` builds one region value from a selection, the material
side and the bounds. The material side is a parameter of its own, and
no start side reaches the region.

- `Selection` and `Chain`: an edge, a face, a chain or points that
  straight lines join, valid by construction. Each degenerate selection
  is refused by name (empty, short, not finite, repeated point, no area,
  self-crossing, two chains that cross).
- `PlanarRegion` holds its work plane and checks that its part walls and
  stock edges partition the boundary of the centre, and that the loops
  are oriented by their nesting.
- The adapter in camcraft-motion (`machining2d/kernel_region.rs`) maps
  the present carriers (a picked area, Contour `Side`, `StartSide`) onto
  the kernel inputs. No old planner calls it: the output does not change.
- Pins: one selection gives one region through the Pocket, Contour and
  pocket-carrier paths; two present disagreements (the Offset band at the
  stock edge, the Pocket sliver filter) are pinned and recorded in
  docs/decisions/4025-kernel-region.md.

feat(pathkernel): the entry and exit stage

K5 of the path kernel (#4023). The entry stage is in
crates/pathkernel/src/entry/ (air, hole, column, material, exit, with
proof, room and stage). EntryStage tries the record's order: the asked
entry outside material, an arc lead from the air (#3746), a pre-drilled
hole, a cleared column, then a helix or a ramp only when the user chose
an entry into material. A plunge is used only when asked and the tool
can plunge. When no entry fits, the stage refuses by name.

EntryPlanner::entry now returns Result<Verdict<Entry>, Refusal>, so an
entry of another kind than asked names its Fallback (law 4). Entry::led
is the single gate: it binds the descent to the proof and a new Lead to
its room. Exit::proved checks the lead-out start and the retract; the
exit leads out where the tool cuts nothing, else it goes straight up.

camcraft-geometry gets geo2d::arc_points and Region::holds_path.
No old planner changes.

fix(pathkernel): the edge strip is stock until a cut clears it; each lift arm named

Review of PR #4234. The link proof counted a centre within 0.1 tool
radius of the stock edge, on either side, as open ground. Inside the
stock such a centre cuts up to 1.1 r into uncut stock, more than the
0.9 r swath that the proof permits. Open ground is now only the air of
the region or the swath of a cut already made; the AIR constant is
removed (the kernel has no sample outside the stock and short of its air).

The lift reasons are now LiftReason values built from the named
constants: no unwrap_or fallback. A path with no finite point lifts with
BAD_PATH, a region that is not planar with NOT_PLANAR_LINK, and the
policy match is exhaustive.

lift counts (disc band 13, dog-bone band 15 on Outside, each named; 0
crossings), and the order pins for a whole full-width curve and the

fix(pathkernel): a link can run outside the stock where the ground is proved

The link proof of the path kernel accepts a sample in the edge band:
outside the stock, within one tool radius of a stock edge, as the entry
stage's legal room defines it. The sample must not be inside the part
zone (the part grown by the tool radius plus the stock to leave) and
must be more than a tool radius from each keep-out area. The stock
inside the edge stays open only within the swath of a cut already made.

The region keeps the part zone of an Outside region, and the air leaves
it out: a part that reaches out of the stock is no longer in the air.
The edge route can also walk along the loops of the air.

Pins: a link in the band over uncut stock (UNCUT_STOCK), near a
keep-out (HITS_FIXTURE), beside a part that reaches out of the stock
(CUTS_PART, and no stay across it in the air), and a link out through
the air and back over cleared stock (stays). The K4 lift counts do not
change; the decision names the missing proof of each disc lift.

Refs #4241

Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

feat(pathkernel): the load control stage

LoadStage implements LoadPlanner for the three load choices. It changes
guide curves only; it adds no entry, link or lift.

- law.rs: the one engagement law. A raster of the stock reader; each
  curve is read in cut order, ae/D = (1 - cos phi) / 2 from the contact
  angle at the rim of the swept disc.
- None: the curves stay; each cut above the stated limit is named, with
  one status line note for each reason.
- ConstantEngagement (Rings): a mid-level ring of the same distance
  field is inserted before a ring that reads above the load; an
  insertion that does not lower the load goes out again and the cut is
  named (the sharp corner of offset rings). The stock reach (Adaptive)
  is refused by name: the HSM planner stays behind the load trait.
- Trochoidal: each FullWidth stretch becomes loops that walk the
  stretch, sized by the free room; where no loop fits, the stretch
  stays and is named.

Pins: the laws suite (load_stage.rs) with the ring planner, the order
stage and the link stage; the motion kernel_laws readings (k3_load.rs).
Follow-up: #4260.

fix(pathkernel): later stages rebuild a curve through its family

The K4 order stage reversed a curve with Curve::new, which refuses the
helix family: a valid helix guide set was refused with the constructor's
reason HELIX_NEEDS_LEAD (review of PR #4244 at 33c116cfa).

One rule for the class: a later stage that restarts, reverses or
replaces a curve makes it again through the constructor of the curve's
family (Curve::with_points: Curve::helix with the same circle and lead,
else Curve::new with the same circle), or refuses by its own reason.

- Order: a helix always runs down its lead (reversed only when the guide
  set holds it upward); a direction that its hand does not give is named
  by the note HELIX_HAND_SETS_DIRECTION. A failed rebuild is the order
  reason NOT_REVERSIBLE.
- Load: constant engagement inserts passes only before a ring
  (NOT_A_RING else); trochoidal loops leave a curve with a lead, an exact
  circle or a changing depth as it is (SHAPE_KEPT); a refused rebuild is
  SET_NOT_KEPT, loops that make no curve LOOPS_NOT_A_CURVE.
- Table test later_stages: each guide family against each later stage;
  the trace chain-region table gets the load stage rows.
- Doc sentence of segment_gap made clear.

commit.message:
test(pathkernel): each law assertion can break, and a refusal is never held

Review of PR #4383, class A. One rule for the class: each law assertion
can break, and a refusal never counts as held.

- kit: a LawVerdict has an Outcome (Held, Broken, Refused(reason)). A
  refused or unread leg is never held; an empty measure list is refused.
  refused_held (0 against 0) is removed.
- registry: KindRecipe registers expected refusals by case and reason;
  law_failures fails each broken law and each unregistered refusal.
- L1: a refused first call is refused; two refusals are not compared by
  their reason text.
- L2: a refused material side is broken; the order leg is never skipped.
- L3, L4, L6, link rule: all-refused or empty legs are refused, not held.
- L5: an IntoMaterial descent onto material must move in the plane or be
  an asked plunge; the stand-in helix is now a real helix.
- L6: the always-held report row is dropped.
- L7: the record is read from a recorded file, not made from the run
  under test.
- refusals.rs: an always-refusing stand-in for each law; no law is held
  on an always-refusing planner set.
- guide_laws: the fixtures get a stock box; L2 had passed on a refused
  Outside side.
